newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bolivar ends firm at 484/485/dlr.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bolivar ends firm at 484/485/dlr.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar closed slightly firmer at 484.00/485.00 per dollar as banks bought bolivars to take advantage of rising interbank lending rates, traders said.
The bolivar closed Monday at 484.25/485.25 per dollar.
Strong corporate dollar demand weakened the bolivar in the morning. "But then it bounced back as banks moved into bolivars due to interest rate pressure in the interbank market," said one trader.

Traders said interbank overnight lending rates rose to between 15 and 40 percent as investors earmarked funds for Wednesday's 70 billion bolivar TEM auction. TEM yields are expected to rise at the auction, having recently topped 20 percent in secondary trade.
Bolivar strength was further helped by strong Central Bank dollar sales, traders added.

Venezuela's foreign exchange market is unusual in that the Central Bank is its largest single supplier of dollars, which blurs the difference between the Central Bank supplying liquidity and intervening.
